how: Reinforcement and defence calls recruit participants around the existing grey field and clown.
Insufficient numbers for policing text make the clown preferable, while another participant scales an ambitious clown back to a logo.
Limited capacity prompts changing the intended representation before any demonstrated relocation after defeat.
Scarce hands can prompt redesign without stopping the project or moving after defeat.
A withdrawn migration prediction and a neighbour moving its face do not establish relocation of the focal room after defeat.
Participants initiate the clown through a proposal followed by a nose anchor and mask-first instructions.
Participants revise the shared design through lettering, additional symbols, goal updates and substituted targets.
Members report lettering placed and lost, while later reports identify completed and missing parts.
A nose coordinate anchors the clown and participants request a map and location before working.
A bare assent accepts the proposal to allow purple HONK without asking anything back.
The direct purple-HONK acceptance supports proposal uptake but cannot establish that silent readers accepted recruiting calls by placing.
Calls and work reports occur, but these concepts do not identify each contribution as caused by a particular call.
A concrete starting coordinate is followed in its reply chain by a call for reinforcements.
A clown proposal receives practical approval and an anchor coordinate, establishing an actionable starting design.
Circulating instructions must be followed by reconciling conflicting corrections when members repair the same features differently.
An actionable map or coordinate does not settle the design when members continue opposing repairs.

statement: Uneven labour within a shared build
how: A shared public project can depend on an exhausted individual working solo overnight on one component.
A coordination complaint, prospective diplomat and theatrical duty claim cannot establish whether formal ordering was decided outside the visible passages.
A conditional offer to run a rewritten defence script establishes willingness rather than actual automated placements.
Requests for bots and conditional script offers leave actual script deployment unresolved.
Defence pressure leads visibly to seeking automation, but the transition to running it requires an available rewritten script and confirmed use.
Members rally, plan continuous upkeep and report repairing damaged eyes, logo, uniform and pants.
Outlining makes an emerging figure recognizable as artwork and reportedly reduces random interference during construction.
A completion-thread reply explicitly turns the standing clown into something that must now be defended.
Members identify internal infighting and unwanted outline placements as sources of conflicting repair.
Repair requires distinguishing competing corrections by fellow participants as well as damage attributed to outsiders.
Participants report permission, accept a colour compromise and negotiate promises against attack.
Negotiated permission can enable completion of the chosen figure before upkeep becomes the main task.
Threatened upkeep is accompanied by participants seeking envoys and reporting nonattack negotiations.
A member reports negotiating with representatives while others offer to carry requests between groups.
Reported permission to complete the clown does not establish sustained residence under a host room's jurisdiction.
A visitor requests defensive help in return for permitted colouring and another participant proposes passing help forward.
The visiting helper explicitly attributes a defensive appeal to the earlier accommodation over HONK's colour.
Defensive assistance is explicitly justified by a returned favour rather than a demonstrated shortage of hands.
Coalition proposals and invitations must be distinguished from completed membership or joint defence.
An alliance proposal and offer to ask leave acceptance and coalition operation unresolved.
Protection motivates proposing an alliance, but no concept confirms that defence produced coalition membership.
Some participants urge avoiding new enemies and offer help moving an obstructing neighbour's face.
Participants can accommodate a displaced neighbour through relocation assistance while continuing to claim its original space.
Negotiation can produce assisted displacement rather than sparing the neighbour's original work in place.

statement: Moving an overlap onto a third neighbour
how: A helper proposes moving the displaced face into another group's orange area because its owners might not notice.
An outside visitor reports their group's stop-invading order, apologizes and promises repair pixels.
A refusal to spare space and a volunteered diplomatic role do not establish dispute over who can bind the room to agreements.
Agreement and divergent spatial preferences do not show an ensuing dispute over authority to commit all placers.
Inherited game lore supplies the duty to build, the grey background's justification and the account of survival.
The lore-based proposal to invade the blue corner supplies no evidence of an earlier quarrel with that target.
Game lore justifies aggression but does not establish a pre-existing tie that made the blue corner a rival.
Fake administrative threats and takeovers run alongside the canvas while replies reveal and evaluate the joke.
A member wants canvas posts to stop flooding the subreddit immediately after celebrating the surviving nose.
Host boundaries also loosen when a moderator expressly permits pure honking inside a celebration thread.
An unrelated advertisement removal and approval joke cannot establish a general canvas-post removal policy.
The ending flood objection establishes dissatisfaction but does not itself identify a particular call's causal role or implemented containment.
Participants celebrate completion, thank helpers, say GG and credit the surviving work as a landmark.
The maker's completion report receives that same maker's direct thanks to everyone who helped.
A post shows the clown's emergence and later posts explicitly mark the canvas's end.
Recording and celebration interleave, so their presence and order do not establish that celebration caused preservation.
A successor-canvas proposal receives a reply preferring a new game symbol over copying the clown.
Post-close successor proposals are visible without demonstrating that a particular saved record caused continuation or that the successor was completed.
The successor-design disagreement does not show dispute over cleaning or correcting a preserved shared canvas.
Participants propose invading the blue corner and later declare encroachment necessary for the wanted sign.
Attack talk shares the build thread without demonstrating that a recruiting call caused actual offensive placements.
An attack proposal receives preparation and build-first advice rather than an unconditional refusal to harm neighbours.
An invasion commitment includes a rebuilding offer, and another participant advocates protecting existing work instead of creating enemies.
A participant reports apparently holding the attackers off, supporting a limited outcome claim rather than a sustained taunting exchange.
A survival claim about the void cannot establish that an earlier blue-corner attack proposal generated a continuing contest with its target.
